Welcome to Maypole School
Maypole School has three school sites, in Streatham (SW16 2QA), Sunbury-on-Thames (TW16 6QE) and Croydon (CR2 7HY). Looking ahead we are planning to open a 4th school in the Croydon area, for pupils in Key Stages 3 / 4, in early 2027.
Our schools are for pupils with social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) difficulties, and most of our pupils will also have some combination of additional complex needs, such as Anxiety, ASD, severe / profound ASD, ADHD, FASD, PDA, OCD, ODD, Toxic Childhood Stress / Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), Attachment difficulties, Developmental Trauma or Delay, Speech and Language difficulties incl severe (non / pre-verbal), Cognition and Learning difficulties, Specific Learning Difficulties such as Dyslexia and Dyspraxia; and more.
Many of our young people will have displayed challenging behaviour at their previous schools. But most no longer do this at Maypole, because they feel safe, and understood. Each of our classes caters for different needs; and we have separate classes for children who should not be in a challenging environment.
We’re passionate about helping these children to succeed at Maypole School, in spite of their very complex needs, and their difficulties at previous schools.
We are family-owned and family-run, and we pride ourselves on delivering better outcomes than other schools manage with similar children, and at lower cost to LAs. Our intent is to provide the best SEMH schools in the South London / SE region.
We say this with confidence because we have a very experienced leadership team, with a proven record of growing highly successful SEMH schools, and of succeeding with children with really complex needs, where all previous schools had been unable to do so.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - What does "therapeutic school" mean, what Therapies does the school provide, and how do we allocate Therapy?
pageCache.text:
What does "therapeutic school" mean, what Therapies does the school provide, and how do we allocate Therapy?
What does "therapeutic school" mean?
Maypole school is naturally a therapeutic environment, due to the warmth of the staff and our nurturing approach. In addition to this, activities such as working with animals (for example, horseriding) can also be highly therapeutic in their own right; and there are many other examples. We provide opportunities for this where appropriate.
What Therapies does the school provide?
In addition to being a therapeutic school as described above, Maypole also offers a range of Therapy programmes, delivered by professional therapists. The therapies we normally provide are Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy and Psychotherapy (such as Art or Music Therapy).
However our approach is that we will provide whatever therapy is required, in accordance with the Therapists’ professional Codes of Conduct, to reduce identified barriers to learning. So if a different type of therapy is necessary, then we would potentially provide it if practical.
Not all of our pupils will need therapy programmes, but our experience is that most children with complex needs make better learning progress if their therapeutic needs are properly understood and addressed.
How do we allocate therapy?
Therapy is allocated according to the needs stated in each child’s EHCP; subject to the professional assessment by the Therapist concerned. In practice, some EHCPs do not include any therapy requirements, even though it would be highly beneficial to the child. In these circumstances we will potentially provide the therapy anyway, but always in accordance with the relevant professional Code of Conduct. All therapy costs are provided for within the core fees for a place at the school, so there is no requirement for any therapy fees authorisation process.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - How will my child be kept safe during School trips?
pageCache.text:
How will my child be kept safe during School trips?
Every school trip is risk assessed, and every child at Maypole has their own unique Student Support Plan, which assesses the risks that the individual pupil faces, and sets out the preventative measures that are necessary to keep the child safe, what environment is needed for them to learn most effectively, and the staffing and other measures that are required to keep each pupil safe at all times, both in the school and when on a trip.
So if 1:1 (or even 2:1) staffing is necessary to keep a child safe when going on a trip ... then that’s what we will provide.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - How will my child get to school, and how do I apply for transport?
pageCache.text:
How will my child get to school, and how do I apply for transport?
How will my child get to school?
Due to the complexity of their needs, most pupils at Maypole will be transported each day to school, and back again, in cars that are arranged and funded by the Local Authority for the area that the child lives in. However, this may not apply if you live close to the school, or if the child is capable of using public transport safely. Please note that it is the LA that will make the decision on whether daily transport will be provided; the School is not in any way involved in this process.
How do I apply for transport?
The Transport system varies according to which Local Authority area you live in, but we recommend that Parents / Carers should initially seek the advice of their child’s Case Manager in the SEN(D) Team in their Local Authority, who will often be able to send them a Transport Request Form.
The Parent / Carer then has to send the completed form back to the LA, and assuming that the provision of transport is agreed, then the LA’s Transport Department will arrange it. Please note that there’s normally no point in applying for transport until the assessment process is complete, and the LA has made their decision to fund the placement; only then will the Transport team be able to act and arrange transport.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - Will I get asked to collect my child early, in the event of challenging behaviour?
pageCache.text:
Will I get asked to collect my child early, in the event of challenging behaviour?
No, this is most unlikely. This is what nearly all other schools will do if a child has a behavioural outburst, because they are not set up to be able to cope with it.
But at Maypole we are organised and staffed so that we can manage the challenging behaviour, calm the situation down, continue the nurturing process, and the school day will continue.

Will my child be excluded for bad behaviour?
As explained above, Maypole’s approach is to manage any challenging or negative behaviour that may occur, and that the school day will then continue, rather than to exclude.
We aim to exclude pupils far less frequently than any other similar school of this type.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - Will my child learn bad behaviour at the school?
pageCache.text:
Will my child learn bad behaviour at the school?
All pupils at Maypole with have some form of social, emotional and / or mental health difficulties, normally with other underlying complex needs. So it is no surprise that many of our pupils will have displayed some form of behavioural difficulties at their previous schools.
This was often because they were in the wrong environment for them, which meant that the previous school was unable to meet their needs.
But at Maypole we can offer many different environments, and each child will be with other pupils who have compatible needs. So Maypole is a school where children’s behaviour will improve, and in many cases will be transformed for the better.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - Class sizes, and staffing ratios
pageCache.text:
Class sizes, and staffing ratios
Class size
We offer an on-site curriculum for Key Stages 1-5 (ages 5-19), tailored to each individual's needs.We have very small classes, with strong staffing support. The largest class will typically be 5 pupils strong, but a few classes may be smaller than this, where this will better meet the children’s complex needs. Where a child is unable (for whatever reason) to learn when alongside other pupils, we have the ability to provide a personal classroom where this is appropriate.
Pupil : staff ratio
We have very small classes, with strong staffing support. Typically our class size will be 5 pupils; typically supported by 2-4 staff in each classroom, with our staff available to support. Overall we have an average of at least 1:1 staffing, directly and indirectly. Occasionally some classes may be smaller or slightly larger than 5 pupils, where this will better meet the children’s complex needs. Where a child is unable (for whatever reason) to learn when alongside other pupils, we can in principle provide a dedicated personal classroom where this is appropriate, when one is available.
We will provide whatever staffing ratio is required, and where necessary we can and will provide 2:1 (or even stronger) staffing, where the complexity of needs requires this. Where very strong staffing is required, this will normally be within the environment of a dedicated personal classroom, to avoid disrupting other pupils' education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - School Uniform and School Meals
pageCache.text:
School Uniform and School Meals
What School Uniform must I provide?
Maypole’s school uniform comprises of a sky blue polo shirt or T-shirt and a navy blue sweat shirt, which the school provides; and black trousers /skirt and black shoes or trainers, which the parents / carers must provide.
An initial issue of 3 shirts and 2 sweat shirts will be provided free of charge; and parents / carers may buy more from the school office.
Breakfast and lunch
We provide breakfast for those who’ve not already had it at home, and lunch for all pupils. Pupils may bring their own packed lunch if they wish, provided it is a healthy meal in accordance with our Food Policy, which can be found on the Policies page of this website.
The school is nut-free, and all dietary requirements are catered for. Halal meals are available; but the school is not pork-free.
Do parents / carers have to pay for school meals?
No. All school meals provided by Maypole School are free of charge.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maypole School - Will my child be physically restrained?
pageCache.text:
Will my child be physically restrained?
All our staff are trained to use physical intervention, using the “PRICE” system, which stands for “Protecting Rights in a Caring Environment”. But physical intervention will only ever be used as the last resort, and we do all we can to prevent it being necessary.
The only circumstances in which we will restrain are in order to keep people safe, to prevent injury to the pupil concerned, to prevent injury to others, to prevent significant damage to or destruction of property, and to prevent significant disruption to the learning of others. In these circumstances we will use physical intervention; but we will do it in as caring, gentle and nurturing way as is possible.
Our full Physical Intervention Policy is available via the Policies page of this website.
